title: The Last Two Sacks
subtitle: Two sacks are missing. The signature on the ledger is yours.
period: 1430s · An original mystery inspired by a real place
fiction_notice: Characters, records, testimony, quantities, and events are fictional. Photos show the site today. The glass roof, signs, and restaurant furnishings are from a later period.

protagonist.name: Yusuf
protagonist.want: Keep the job he worked hard to earn
protagonist.need: Own his mistake instead of hiding behind someone else’s name

cast.name: Cem
cast.bond: He vouched for you and got you into the records room.

cast.name: Halime
cast.role: Kitchen helper taking a break by the fountain
cast.bond: She saw where the sacks went, but will not sign a blank record.

cast.name: The steward
cast.role: Checks the accounts before supplies go out
cast.bond: He trusts signed records, not spoken excuses.

evidence.name: Morning delivery ledger
evidence.text: Delivered: 12 sacks. Your entry: 12 sacks of grain received. Signed: Yusuf. A margin note says “check the types of goods.” You left it out of the official ledger.

evidence.name: Loading slip
evidence.text: 10 sacks of grain; 2 sacks of flour. Total: 12. Cem says the flour went straight to the imaret, not the grain store.

evidence.name: Halime’s signed statement
evidence.text: I received two sacks of flour from Cem and took them to the imaret. I will sign this statement if you leave your own name in the original ledger.

evidence.name: Kitchen receipt
evidence.text: Received: 2 sacks of flour. Delivery name: blank. The kitchen clerk signed. The grain store holds 10 sacks. Nothing is missing, but we still need a witness to identify the carrier.

evidence.name: Reconciliation sheet
evidence.text: 12 delivered = 10 sacks of grain + 2 sacks of flour at the kitchen. Nothing is missing. Your official ledger recorded both goods as grain.

scenes.title: Your Name Is on the Ledger
scenes.goal: Find the two sacks before supplies go out. Start with the ledger you signed.

opening.speaker: The steward
opening.text: The ledger says twelve sacks. The grain store has ten. Cem handled the delivery. Give me an answer I can put in the record before supplies go out.

opening.speaker: Yusuf · You
opening.text: I have been a clerk for seven days. Cem vouched for me. If I blame him, the numbers add up—and I might keep my job.

task.prompt: Open the morning ledger. What did you actually sign?

after.speaker: You
after.text: “Check the types of goods.” I remember that note, but the official ledger says only “grain.” Find Cem at the madrasa.

scenes.title: The One Who Vouched for You
scenes.goal: Use the photo to find Cem’s meeting place. Then decide whether to buy him time.

opening.speaker: Cem
opening.text: There were two kinds of goods. Grain went to the store; flour went to the kitchen. I left the loading slip by the octagonal pool, across from the classroom. Read it before you let them take me.

task.prompt: Find the octagonal pool across from the classroom. Tap a numbered spot on the photo or choose a spot below.

hotspots.label: White pool in the courtyard
hotspots.text: An octagonal marble pool, shown at the courtyard’s center in the publication. You found the meeting place, but that does not prove who moved the sacks.

hotspots.label: Tall arch ahead
hotspots.text: The teaching iwan faces the courtyard. Use it as another landmark.

hotspots.label: Glass roof above
hotspots.text: The steel-and-glass roof was added later. It is not a clue from the 1430s.

after.speaker: You
after.text: The slip says ten sacks of grain and two of flour. Did I copy the total as grain? But did the flour reach the kitchen?

decision.prompt: A guard is closing in. Cem grabs your sleeve.

options.label: Vouch for him in your own name
options.detail: Buy two more minutes to check the records. You take responsibility, and Cem stays with you.

options.label: Let the guard take him for now
options.detail: Keep time to check the accounts. The slip stays behind, but Cem cannot help you.

scenes.title: The Two Cup Niches
scenes.goal: Find the fountain’s two cup niches. Help Halime serve water so she can stay and give her statement.

opening.speaker: Halime
opening.text: Two sacks of flour? I saw them. But tell me: do you want the truth, or just a signature for your ledger?

opening.speaker: Halime
opening.text: First, find the shared cups—one on the left and one on the right. Help me serve the people here, and I’ll go with you to the kitchen.

task.prompt: Find the two small niches in the brickwork where the shared cups go.

hotspots.label: Square niche on the left
hotspots.text: Left cup niche. The publication describes both niches as places for drinking cups, not hidden storage.

hotspots.label: Square niche on the right
hotspots.text: Right cup niche. People could take water and share cups here. The scene about serving visitors is fictional.

hotspots.label: Panel and spout below
hotspots.text: The spout and brickwork are shown as they look today. This photo cannot tell us how the water system worked in the story’s time.

after.speaker: You
after.text: I point out both niches. Halime still will not sign. “If you can own your mistake, then I can put my name to this.”

decision.prompt: The accounts are nearly due. Will you stay and help her?

options.label: Stay and ask her to sign with you
options.detail: Get a statement identifying the delivery person. It costs time and may make you late.

options.label: Ask where the kitchen is and hurry on
options.detail: Keep tracking the goods, but she will not identify the delivery person.

scenes.title: The Kitchen Missing from the Ledger
scenes.goal: Find the star pattern to locate the story’s receipt. Then sort the two goods into the right records.

opening.speaker: Kitchen helper
opening.text: The person who brought the flour left the receipt by the star above the window. We received two sacks, but the slip does not say who brought them.

opening.speaker: You
opening.text: If we check only the grain store, the kitchen might as well not exist. Meals do not appear by themselves on a page.

task.prompt: Find the star pattern above the window. The modern sign is not a story clue.

hotspots.label: Patterned brick above the narrow window
hotspots.text: The star and geometric brickwork are features recorded in the publication. The receipt’s hiding place is fictional; no artifact is hidden here.

hotspots.label: Black sign
hotspots.text: A later restaurant sign. Do not use modern lettering to interpret events in the 1430s.

hotspots.label: Wooden door
hotspots.text: This is the entrance shown in a modern photo. It is not a surveyed route for historical deliveries.

after.speaker: You
after.text: The kitchen received two sacks of flour. Compare the loading slip, grain count, and kitchen receipt. Do not rely on one total.

sorting.success: 12 = 10 + 2. Nothing is missing. You put two kinds of goods in one column.

scenes.title: The Blank Line
scenes.goal: Present an account others can check. Your name will stay on the page. Cem’s fate depends on what you keep.

opening.speaker: You
opening.text: They were in the kitchen all along. I recorded the wrong goods. I could copy a clean page and remove the morning ledger. Then no one would know.

task.prompt: Choose the three records that account for all 12 sacks. Place them on the review board.

after.speaker: The steward
after.text: Nothing is missing. Now tell me: what happens to the original ledger—and to the apprentice?

options.label: Keep the original. Sign a correction.
options.detail: Correct the stock record. Halime’s statement may clear Cem at once. Your probation will be reviewed.

options.label: Remove the original and submit a clean copy
options.detail: Keep your job for now, but hide the source of the error. Cem will still face questions.

options.label: Blame the kitchen for a missing entry
options.detail: Hide your mistake. The kitchen staff will be investigated, and meal service may be disrupted.
